overview.title: Inspecting batches and fitting with ModelCheckpoint
overview.section: 8.2 Training a convnet from scratch on a small dataset
overview.main_topic: Checking the shapes yielded by the image Dataset, then training the ConvNet for 50 epochs with validation monitoring and a ModelCheckpoint callback that keeps the best model by validation loss
overview.central_idea: The training Dataset yields (images, labels) batches of shape (batch, 180, 180, 3) and (batch,); fit() takes the training and validation Datasets directly, and ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True, monitor="val_loss") ensures the saved file always holds the epoch with the lowest validation loss, so overfitting later in training does not require retraining.
overview.importance: This is the first actual training run of the chapter and establishes the baseline (about 80% accuracy, p.265). The checkpoint-the-best-epoch pattern is a practical alternative to rerunning training with fewer epochs, which the book did in earlier chapters.
learning_objectives: Inspect the shapes of a Dataset batch with a for loop and break
Pass Dataset objects to fit() for training and validation
Configure ModelCheckpoint with filepath, save_best_only and monitor
Explain why saving the best epoch by val_loss protects against overfitting

summary:
The page closes the tf.data detour ("You're about to see more `map()` action over the next chapters") and begins **Fitting the model**.

First, the authors inspect one batch of `train_dataset` (**listing 8.14**): iterating with `for data_batch, labels_batch in train_dataset:` and breaking after one step prints `data batch shape: (32, 180, 180, 3)` and `labels batch shape: (32,)` — 180×180 RGB images and integer labels. The text says there are 32 samples per batch, the batch size; note, however, that listing 8.9 set `batch_size = 64`, so running the code as printed would show 64 (see the review flag).

Next, **listing 8.15** trains the model. `fit()` receives `train_dataset` directly (labels come from the dataset), runs for `epochs=50`, and uses `validation_data=validation_dataset` to compute validation metrics on a separate `Dataset` at the end of each epoch.

The key addition is a **`ModelCheckpoint` callback**, configured with `filepath="convnet_from_scratch.keras"`, `save_best_only=True` and `monitor="val_loss"`. It saves the model after an epoch only if `val_loss` is lower than at any previous time, overwriting the previous file. Consequently the saved file always contains the model state from the best-performing epoch on validation data. The payoff, as the authors put it: if the model starts overfitting, we don't need to retrain it for fewer epochs — we just reload the saved file. (Earlier in the book, the approach was to note the best epoch and retrain from scratch.)

The returned `history` object records per-epoch metrics; the page ends by announcing plots of training/validation loss and accuracy in **figure 8.9** (p.275), which will show clear overfitting.

paragraphs.excerpt: Let’s fit the model on our dataset. We use the validation_data argument
paragraphs.what_it_says: The model is fit on the dataset, with validation_data used to monitor validation metrics on a separate Dataset.
paragraphs.what_it_means: At the end of each epoch Keras evaluates the model on validation_dataset, producing val_loss and val_accuracy in the logs and history.

paragraphs.excerpt: Note that we also use a ModelCheckpoint callback to save the model
paragraphs.what_it_says: A ModelCheckpoint callback saves the model after each epoch, but with save_best_only=True and monitor="val_loss" it writes a new file only when val_loss improves on all previous values, overwriting the old one. The file thus always holds the best epoch by validation performance, so after overfitting you can reload it instead of retraining for fewer epochs.
paragraphs.what_it_means: Training runs for the full 50 epochs, but the best snapshot is retained automatically. It works like keeping a running minimum: best = min(best, val_loss_t), saving whenever a new minimum is found.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Saves a full second training run and guarantees the evaluated model (p.275) is the pre-overfitting one.
paragraphs.technical_idea: Selecting the epoch by validation loss slightly overfits to the validation set, which is why the final measurement is on the separate test set.

concepts.name: ModelCheckpoint callback
concepts.definition: A Keras callback that saves the model during training, optionally only when a monitored metric improves.
concepts.intuition: An automatic 'save game' that only overwrites your save when you've done better.
concepts.technical: filepath="convnet_from_scratch.keras", save_best_only=True, monitor="val_loss" → file updated whenever val_loss reaches a new minimum.
concepts.significance: Keeps the best-epoch model so overfitting later in training costs nothing.
concepts.misconception: The final model object in memory after fit() is the last-epoch model, not the best one; you must reload the file.

concepts.name: Validation monitoring
concepts.definition: Evaluating on held-out data after each epoch via validation_data.
concepts.intuition: A practice exam taken after each study session.
concepts.technical: Produces val_loss/val_accuracy logs, used here by ModelCheckpoint.
concepts.significance: Enables detection of overfitting and best-epoch selection.
concepts.misconception: Validation data never update the weights, but decisions based on them can still leak information.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.definition: When performance on training data keeps improving while validation performance stalls or worsens.
concepts.intuition: Memorizing the training examples instead of learning general features.
concepts.technical: Detected by val_loss reaching a minimum and rising/stalling while training loss falls.
concepts.significance: Expected with 2,000 training images and no regularization; the checkpoint guards against it.
concepts.example: See figure 8.9 on p.275: validation loss minimal after ~10 epochs.
concepts.misconception: Training longer always gives a better model.

concepts.name: Dataset as fit() input
concepts.definition: Passing a tf.data.Dataset that yields (inputs, labels) to fit().
concepts.intuition: The dataset supplies both x and y.
concepts.technical: No y or batch_size arguments needed; batching is the dataset's job.
concepts.misconception: Passing batch_size to fit() with a Dataset has no effect on the batching.

math.title: save_best_only rule
math.source_text: only save a new file ... when the current value of the val_loss metric is lower than at any previous time during training

variables.meaning: validation loss at the end of epoch t

math.operations: Compare current validation loss with the running minimum.
math.purpose: Formalizes the checkpoint condition described in the text.
math.interpretation: The saved file corresponds to \(\arg\min_t \text{val\_loss}_t\) at the end of training.
math.intuition: Keep a running record; only replace it when beaten.
math.numerical_example: val_loss = [0.69, 0.64, 0.60, 0.61, 0.57, 0.59, …]: saves at epochs 1, 2, 3, 5; epochs 4 and 6 are not saved.

code.title: Fitting the model using a Dataset
code.original_code:
callbacks = [
    keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath="convnet_from_scratch.keras",
        save_best_only=True,
        monitor="val_loss",
    )
]
history = model.fit(
    train_dataset,
    epochs=50,
    validation_data=validation_dataset,
    callbacks=callbacks,
)
code.what_it_does: Trains the ConvNet for 50 epochs on the training dataset, evaluates on the validation dataset after each epoch, and saves the model whenever val_loss reaches a new minimum.

line_explanations.explanation: A list with one ModelCheckpoint callback: save to convnet_from_scratch.keras, only when val_loss improves.
fit() takes the Dataset directly; it supplies both images and labels.
Validation metrics computed each epoch on validation_dataset.
history.history stores per-epoch loss, accuracy, val_loss, val_accuracy for plotting (p.275).

code.inputs_outputs: Inputs: compiled model, two datasets. Outputs: trained model in memory (last epoch), best model on disk, History object.

code.theory_link: Early-stopping-like model selection by validation loss.

deeper.title: Checkpointing vs. retraining
deeper.body: Beyond the book: before callbacks, the workflow was (1) train long, (2) read the best epoch off the validation curve, (3) retrain from scratch for that many epochs. That doubles the cost and, because of random initialization and shuffling, the retrained model isn't even the same one. ModelCheckpoint with save_best_only keeps the actual best weights from the single run. EarlyStopping can additionally stop wasting epochs once val_loss has not improved for a while.

deeper.title: Why monitor val_loss and not val_accuracy?
deeper.body: Inference: val_loss is a smooth, continuous measure of how well-calibrated the predicted probabilities are, while val_accuracy on 1,000 images moves in steps of 0.1% and can plateau while the loss is changing. The loss is what the model optimizes, so it is the more sensitive indicator of overfitting. Monitoring val_accuracy is also valid but would select a possibly different epoch.

misconceptions.claim: After fit() with save_best_only=True, the model variable holds the best weights.
misconceptions.correction: It holds the last-epoch weights; the best ones are in the saved file, which must be reloaded (p.275).

misconceptions.claim: ModelCheckpoint stops training when val_loss stops improving.
misconceptions.correction: It only saves; training continues for all 50 epochs. EarlyStopping is the callback that stops training.

misconceptions.claim: The batch size here is necessarily 32.
misconceptions.correction: The printed output says 32, but listing 8.9 sets batch_size = 64; the actual shape depends on that setting.

questions.question: With save_best_only=True and monitor="val_loss", when does ModelCheckpoint write the file?
options: Only when val_loss is lower than at any previous epoch
After every epoch regardless of performance
Only at the end of training
questions.answer: Only when val_loss is lower than at any previous epoch
questions.explanation: That is the condition stated on the page. Saving every epoch is the behavior without save_best_only; it doesn't wait for the end, and training accuracy isn't monitored.

questions.question: What are the shapes printed by listing 8.14, and what does each axis mean?
questions.answer: (32, 180, 180, 3): batch, height, width, RGB channels; (32,): one integer label per image.
questions.explanation: As printed; note listing 8.9 set batch_size = 64, which would give 64 in the first axis.

questions.question: Why does the checkpoint mean 'we won't have to retrain a new model for a lower number of epochs if we start overfitting'?
questions.answer: The file already contains the weights from the epoch with the best validation loss, i.e. the state before overfitting, so we can reload it instead of rerunning training with fewer epochs.

questions.question: What role does validation_data=validation_dataset play in fit()?
options: It computes validation metrics at the end of each epoch
It is merged with the training data
questions.answer: It computes validation metrics at the end of each epoch
questions.explanation: The page: it monitors validation metrics on a separate Dataset. It is never used for training, and has nothing to do with the learning rate or shuffling.

questions.question: Given val_loss per epoch [0.70, 0.63, 0.65, 0.58, 0.60, 0.59], at which epochs does the callback save, and which epoch's model is in the file at the end?
questions.answer: Saves at epochs 1, 2 and 4; the file holds epoch 4 (val_loss 0.58).
questions.explanation: A save happens only when val_loss is a new minimum.

questions.question: After listing 8.15 finishes, which weights does the variable model contain, and what should you evaluate on the test set?
questions.answer: model contains the epoch-50 (likely overfit) weights; you should reload convnet_from_scratch.keras and evaluate that.
questions.explanation: The checkpoint is on disk; p.275 reloads it before evaluation.

questions.question: Can you explain why monitoring val_loss rather than training loss is necessary for picking the best model?
questions.answer: Training loss keeps decreasing even while the model overfits; only validation loss reflects generalization.
questions.explanation: Self-check linking this page to the overfitting curves on p.275.
